Hi Samir,

Appreciate the clear ask — attaching a compact rate card and a short crosswalk summary to get you started. High level notes (very condensed):

- Hosted API (baseline): pay-as-you-go per token; good for low-to-moderate volume and fastest time-to-value. Typical list rates vary by model size — example baseline for our curated open model SKU: $0.030 / 1k prompt tokens and $0.060 / 1k completion tokens.

- Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity + lower per-token runtime for heavy steady throughput. Commercials typically include a monthly reserved capacity fee (covers GPU pool + platform) + usage discounts on the hosted rate once you hit committed throughput. No per-request SLA unless in Dedicated contract; SLA available as add-on.

- Private (VPC/on-prem): licensing or platform fee, one-time deployment/integration professional services, optional support/patching subscription. Unit inference cost depends on customer hardware and quantization choices; we provide a modeled TCO.

Attached: Redwood-Rate-Card-2026.pdf (compact baseline) and a starter TCO worksheet we can tailor. I'll loop in our pricing/solutions team internally to build the dedicated vs private line items you requested.

Would you prefer a short 30-min call this week to walk procurement through the summary?

Best,
Marissa Cole

Samir / Janet,

Thanks for the ask — attached are two files: a compact rate card (Redwood-Rate-Card-2026.pdf) and a tailored Dedicated-TCO-worksheet.xlsx with ballpark numbers we discussed. Executive summary below to share with procurement:

Executive summary (one page):
- Hosted API (baseline): pay-as-you-go; example list prices for the curated open model: $0.030 / 1k prompt tokens, $0.060 / 1k completion tokens. Best when you want no upfront commitment and rapid integration.

- Dedicated: typical commercial structure = monthly reserved capacity fee + discounted usage. Example math (4x GPU reserved): $30k/mo reserved + blended usage that equates to ~20% lower effective per-token cost vs hosted at 70% utilization. Reserved capacity guarantees throughput and isolates your workload. Minimum committed term commonly 12 months for Dedicated.

- Private (VPC/on-prem): one-time deployment/professional services + platform license (example range $100k–$350k one-time depending on scope) + annual support (e.g., $20k–$80k). Unit inference cost depends on customer hardware — we modeled a conservative case in the worksheet assuming modern on-prem GPUs + int8 quantization: Private can reach 30–50% lower unit inference cost vs hosted, but requires upfront CapEx and ops investment.

Discounting guidance: 12-month commitments and token-volume commitments are the primary levers. Typical committed volume discounts for steady high-volume customers in Dedicated are 15–35% off hosted list depending on term and utilization. Private deals usually include an enterprise license negotiation that folds in lower per-unit assumptions and larger PS fees.

Next steps:
- Review the attached worksheet and let us know which Dedicated configuration (GPU count, redundancy, region) you want us to model precisely.
- If procurement wants, we can run a 30-min pricing walkthrough Fri 2/27 or Mon 3/1.

Attachments: Redwood-Rate-Card-2026.pdf, Dedicated-TCO-worksheet.xlsx

Best,
Marissa Cole

Samir / Procurement team — answers inline below.

1) Dedicated mapping to token throughput: using the 4x GPU reserved example with a blended utilization model, the ~20% effective per-token saving corresponds to roughly 80–100M tokens/month sustained (70% utilization). For your 120M tokens/month baseline we model a blended saving of ~22–28% depending on request size distribution and KV cache hit rates. We'll run your exact prompt/completion mix if you share sample token distributions.

2) Private licensing model: the range I gave assumes customer-hosted deployment where Acme owns the runtime instances (perpetual-style license + onboarding PS). We offer a Redwood-managed appliance option (we maintain images/patching) as an alternative subscription — that option typically increases OPEX but reduces engineering lift. Data residency: Private (VPC/on-prem) keeps logs and KV caches in your network; we ingest only what you authorize into Redwood control plane for billing/rollups. We can add contract language to guarantee log residency and KMS integration.

3) Lead times & staging: typical on-prem deployment lead time is 6–10 weeks from SOW signature for a standard rollout (networking, security review, install, validation). We provide a staging environment in a customer VPC or a sandbox cluster we manage for shorter proofs-of-concept (2–3 weeks) depending on networking approvals.

Next steps proposed:
- I'll schedule a 30-min pricing and SOW walk-through for Tue 3/3 at 10am PT (tentative).
- If procurement wants a tailored TCO with your exact token distribution, please send the sample usage CSV and we'll run it through the worksheet.
